text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif directed provincial governments to take immediate steps to curb lawlessness and demanded "better coordination among various agencies" to deal with the problem effectively.
- After the recovery of eight more bodies, the death toll in Wednesday's building collapse in Karachi rose to 10.
- Another 92 people were taken into custody in Lahore amid a police crackdown on religious militants to curb sectarian violence.
- Interior Minister Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain told the Senate (upper house) the government plans to hold a population census this year "in consonance with constitutional requirements".
- Japan has taken serious exception to Islamabad's unilateral decision to abort in midstream a Japanese project of assistance to the state-run Pakistan Railways.

- Interior Minister Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain denied the government had struck a secret deal with the U.S. authorities to allow the arrest and extradition of Aimal Kansi, suspected of killing two CIA officials outside CIA headquarters.

- A foreign office spokesman described Pakistan's recent successful launching of its Hatf III rocket as "peaceful routine experiment" and denied that Chinese technological assistance was being used to develop upper atmospheric research missile technology.
- The state's Central Board of Revenue has started scrutinising the affairs of 11,340 industrial units that deposited about half as much sales tax in 1996/97 as they had in 1995/96.
- Production at most factories making airconditioners, televisions, bicycles and pig iron in Punjab province and North West Frontier Province has declined in the last three years.
- Pakistan's liquid foreign exchange reserves rose by $121 million to $1.16 billion in the week ending June 28, the State (central) Bank of Pakistan said.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The Asian Developmewnt Bank has agreed in principle to provide $200 million to the state-run Water and Power Development Authority for a flood protection project.
- Britain's Overseas Development Administration is likely to increase its support to the social action programme to $48 million from $20 million.
- The government has decided to provide an $8.0 million revolving fund and arrange 3.5 billion rupees bridge financing for the early completion of Ghazi Barotha Hydel power project.
- The government is to formulate a consumer protection law against possible exploitation by business monopolies.
- The private Pakistan Credit Rating Agency has upgraded the long-term rating of Askari Commercial Bank Ltd from A to AA, in recognition of its sound financial position and outstanding performance.
- State-run Pakistan National Shipping Corporation announced it has returned to profit after several years of heavy losses.
FINANCIAL POST

- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has issued fresh instructions to state-run banks to speed up recovery of bad debts of over 100 billion rupees and has set a deadline of December 6, 1997 to clear all defaults.
THE NATION
- Opposition leader Benazir Bhutto demanded the immediate prosecution and unseating of Nawaz Sharif for allegedly filing false declaration of assets as a National Assembly member.
THE MUSLIM
- The government will file another reference against former prime minister Benazir Bhutto, her husband Asif Ali Zardari and a businessman for serious irregularities in exporting urea to India.
THE NEWS
- Interior Minister Chaudhry Shujjat Hussain denied that the govenment has allowed the FBI to open an office in Islamabad.
